If you could go back to the early days of the internet, would you handle your privacy differently? Most of us would. We would be more careful about which services we joined and what information we shared. Since a time machine isn't an option, we have to face reality. Your personal data is being bought and sold publicly right now.

Right now, your phone number, email address, home address, and even your family relationships are being packaged and sold to marketers, insurance companies, and hackers. While Apple's built-in privacy protections in Safari and Mail can block some tracking as you browse, they cannot erase information that has been scraped and spread to hundreds of intermediary databases over the years. Data brokers have built a multi-billion-dollar industry by collecting, packaging, and selling your digital data. It's time to take your personal information off the market and the internet. Let's look at how to do it.

The security risks posed by data brokers

However, the danger goes far beyond annoying spam calls. When your information is readily available, you become an easy target for sophisticated cyberattacks. Since this industry is largely unregulated, your most private information and details—including past employment, places you've lived, old loans, and more—can be easily purchased. This poses a significant security concern.

Modern scammers use broker data to craft highly personalized and hard-to-spot phishing attacks. When a scammer already knows your job title, where you've lived before, or the names of your colleagues and friends, they can easily bypass your defensive instincts. If a scammer knows you in detail, they only need to strike when your guard is down, and their chances of success increase significantly.

For those concerned about personal safety, these websites and brokers function as a searchable public database that facilitates the work of harassers and stalkers. By mapping the network of relationships between your friends, family, and neighbors, brokers provide a targeting blueprint for people who intentionally keep a low profile and hide their whereabouts.

The solution: Incogni automated data removal service

This ecosystem is massive and, frankly, daunting. Requesting removal from hundreds of sites one by one is practically a full-time job with a very low success rate—because if it were easy, these brokers would already be out of business. What you need is a solution that knows how this industry works and understands its ins and outs, helping you reclaim your right to privacy.

This is exactly why services like Incogni have become so vital to your life, both in the digital world and the real world. This service transforms the major problem you face—your data being everywhere and being sold—into a solved problem, taking a one-stop-shop approach. You don't need to spend months tracking down data brokers one by one; Incogni handles those repetitive and tedious opt-out correspondence procedures on your behalf automatically. They ensure your data isn't just removed once, but is maintained continuously, because brokers will inevitably try to scrape and collect your information again.

Incogni's comprehensive dashboard lets you track the progress of your personal data removal in real time, including:

  • The number of databases that may hold your information

The real benefits of data removal for the privacy-conscious

Removing your information from internet broker databases delivers immediate results for you and your family

  • When companies can't buy your number, scam calls and spam texts will decrease.
  • Scammers lose their targeting leads. Identity thieves often obtain victim information from broker sites.
  • Your home address stays private, making it harder for stalkers and harassers to find where you live.
  • Your credit score stays healthy, as reduced data exposure lowers the risk of identity theft and strengthens your overall financial health.
